about: The retrieval set (Phase 3 step 4, build step 4; 2026-11-23). Each query is worded the way the agent's answers describe what they measured: its column names and phrasing ('pinned at', 'stays flat', 'jumped', 'not the bottleneck'), taken from the tuning runs' root causes and evidence notes, not from the runbooks' text. No figures from any window: no versions, commits, authors, times, counts, or measured values. 'expect' is the runbook that fits, or null where none does. Fixed before the first search (committed first), and never changed to fit a result.

sources.pool: the tuning runs' answers on the three db_pool_exhaustion alarms (pool-1027-1856, -1900, -1901), sweeps 20261113T201129Z to 20261114T221926Z
sources.deploy: the tuning runs' answers on the six bad_deploy alarms (deploy-1027-1905 to deploy-1113-0257), the same sweeps
sources.downstream: the 10 answers on the two downstream_timeout alarms in the 2026-11-17/18 test sweeps, its only runs; decision 12 moves those spent alarms to tuning
sources.neighbor: no runs: never injected. The agent's vocabulary from the runs above, describing what that fault would measure
sources.none: symptoms no runbook covers, in the same vocabulary

queries.query: pool wait p99 jumped and active connections are pinned at the pool max while concurrent requests are well above it; database query time stays flat and no requests fail yet
a config change lowered POOL_MAX_SIZE just before the alarm; requests queue for a connection and pool wait becomes most of request latency
requests on every route fail with TimeoutError acquiring connection from pool after waiting the full acquire timeout; the error rate climbs each minute
latency alarm: p99 over the threshold, and the time is spent waiting for a pool slot, not in the database; payments-api latency is normal
the error rate started rising minutes after pool wait began climbing; the failing lines show pool_wait_time_ms at the acquire timeout and a smaller pool_max_size than before
connections pinned at a small pool size while concurrency rises; the database itself is not slow, so requests are waiting for a connection, not for their queries
500s on all routes from a pool-acquisition timeout raised in the database connection code; the failing version has been live for days, so no code deploy is involved
the error rate jumped from zero within seconds of a new deploy; every failing line is the same TypeError with a stack trace, served by the new version
500s on POST /checkout only, all served by the newly deployed version; latency, pool wait and payments-api stay normal
the failures are specific to checkouts with has_promo false; requests that carry a promo still succeed on the new release
a release went out seconds before the errors began; failing requests return 500 in milliseconds, before any database or payments call
the same exception in a pricing function on every failing request, all on the new version and none on the old one
a steady share of checkouts fails with an unhandled exception since the deploy; the error alarm fired while the latency and pool-wait alarms stayed OK
the only change right before the new errors is a deploy; the earlier config changes are hours old and touch other code paths, so they are not the cause
payments-api p99 jumped in the same minute checkout p99 rose; checkout's own pool wait and DB query time stay flat
POST /checkout requests spend most of their latency waiting on payments-api, and some hit the upstream timeout and return 504 UpstreamTimeout
latency only on POST /checkout while /products and /cart/items stay normal; payments timeouts appear for the first time
the dependency became slow, not this service: upstream_latency_ms accounts for most of latency_ms in the slow requests, and no deploy or config change fits the onset
latency alarm with no failed requests at first; payments_p99_ms climbs toward the upstream timeout
checkout calls to the payments service slowed sharply; the connection pool never queues, so pool exhaustion is ruled out
db_query_p50_ms rose on every route along with pool wait; connections stay busy longer and payments-api is normal
queries are slow once a connection is acquired: query time climbed across all routes, not just checkout, and latency followed it
the request rate rose sharply, with concurrent_max and pool_active_max rising in proportion; err% stays at zero and p50 is unchanged
req climbed and then levelled off while callers say requests fail, with nothing in this service's logs; concurrent_max stays well under the concurrency cap and latency is normal
concurrent_max is flat at the function's concurrency cap; req stopped rising while callers keep sending, and the requests that do run are slow
callers get errors this service never logs, err% stays low, and concurrency is pinned at the reserved limit
a steady stream of cold starts at steady traffic; requests vanish without log lines, err% stays low, and pool and payments-api are flat
instances keep restarting hours after a release; callers see failures that leave no line, and the failures started long after the deploy
requests fail with AccessDenied when checkout-api writes orders, right after a permissions change; latency and pool wait are normal
checkout returns 200 but orders are saved twice; duplicate orders in the table, no errors and normal latency
one client is getting 400 responses for malformed request bodies; no other client is affected
GET /products is slow on its own while database query time, pool wait and payments-api are all flat
